svg.title: Amazon CloudWatch
svg.desc: Amazon CloudWatch. Metrics, logs, alarms and dashboards for AWS resources and your applications, in one monitoring service. Step 1, Where it sits: AWS services publish metrics; apps send logs and EMF metrics; alarms page and scale; people look. Step 2, Metrics and logs: A metric is a namespace, a name and dimensions, kept per 1-min period; EMF log lines become metrics. Step 3, Alarms and actions: p99 hits 1.4 s in 3 of 5 one-minute periods: ALARM, SNS pages on-call; the CPU alarm adds tasks. Step 4, Limits and costs: Each dimension combination is a billed metric; logs cost per GB and never expire by default.

g.text: AWS services publish metrics; apps send logs and EMF metrics; alarms page and scale; people look.
A metric is a namespace, a name and dimensions, kept per 1-min period; EMF log lines become metrics.
p99 hits 1.4 s in 3 of 5 one-minute periods: ALARM, SNS pages on-call; the CPU alarm adds tasks.
Each dimension combination is a billed metric; logs cost per GB and never expire by default.
the EMF line, and a query
rolled up as data ages · under 1 min: kept 3 hours
billed by the hour while the alarm exists
Standard class · retention set per group
Infrequent Access class: no EMF, no metric or
Runs only as an AWS service. Queries:
logs: Insights QL, OpenSearch PPL or SQL
Newer: OTel metrics over OTLP, with PromQL
per account and Region · AWS metrics need no setup
The ALB, Lambda and ECS publish metrics on their own; Lambda and Catalog send logs, and Catalog’s JSON log lines carry a custom metric.
Alarms turn thresholds into actions: a page through SNS, more ECS tasks. Dashboards and Logs Insights queries let people look.
standard resolution 1 min · high resolution 1 s (custom metrics only)
Each request adds a TargetResponseTime sample; for each 1-minute period CloudWatch keeps statistics such as SampleCount, Average and p99.
The EMF line stays in /ecs/catalog and becomes the metric AcmeShop › OrderLatency (Service=catalog); Logs Insights counts ERROR lines.
M OUT OF N, THEN ACTIONS
actions run on state changes; Auto Scaling actions repeat every minute
p99 climbs to 1.4 s: 3 of the last 5 one-minute periods are over 1 s, so latency goes OK → ALARM; 5xx breach too, so impact pages on-call.
CPU at 85% against a 60% target: target tracking’s alarm has ECS run 5 tasks instead of 3. An anomaly band can replace the fixed 1 s.
WHAT IT COSTS, HOW LONG IT KEEPS
Each dimension combination is a billed metric: userId on OrderLatency makes 50,000. Logs cost $0.50/GB in and $0.03/GB-month stored.
Metrics roll up to 5 min after 15 days and 1 h after 63, and expire at 15 months; log groups never expire unless you set a retention.
